To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a novel high molecular weight myosin light-chain kinase is expressed in endothelium.
a novel, high molecular-weight myo-sin light chain kinase is preferentially expressed in endothelium.
a unique high molecular-weight myo-sin light chain kinase is expressed in endothelium and is the only MLCK expressed in endothelial cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the characterization and regulation of a novel high-molecular weight nonmuscle myo-sin light chain kinase isoform expressed in endothelium and its role in the regulation of endothelial cell permeability and junctional gap formation.
the molecular basis of EC barrier function.
the molecular mechanisms that regulate EC junctional integrity and permeability
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the EC MLCK is the only myosin light kinase expressed in human endothelial tissue.
the EC MLCK is a novel isoform of the MLCK family that is expressed exclusively in endothelium and may play an important role in EC contraction and junctional gap formation.
the high molecular-weight endothelial MLCK isoform is expressed in endothelium and is not expressed in smooth muscle or skeletal muscle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have cloned a novel high molecular weight MLCK isoform, which is expressed exclusively in endothelium and may play a role in endothelial cell junctional gap formation, and that we have developed antibodies against this novel isoform.

the EC MLCK is a novel high molecular weight isoform that may be preferentially and exclusively expressed in endothelium and may play a critical role in EC junctional gap formation, cell contraction and barrier function.
endothelial cells express only one isoform of MLCK, a 214-kD isoform, which is different from the 130- to 150-kD isoforms found in smooth muscle cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
endothelial cells express a unique high molecular-weight myo-sin light chain kinase isoform that is distinct from smooth muscle and skeletal muscle myosin light-chain kinase isoforms.
the EC MLCK appears to be expressed only in EC and not in any other tissue type, suggesting that the enzyme is an endothelial cell-specific isoform.

the high molecular-weight isoform of MLCK, which is expressed in endothelium and is distinct from smooth muscle isoforms, may have a specific and critical function in endothelial cell junctional dynamics.
